title: Founding Engineer (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
The opportunity

Tax advisory runs on structured data, recurring work and clear rules, and almost none of it has been rebuilt with modern software. What decides who gets there first is real case data and engineers who build next to the people doing the work.

Vogel advises several thousand mid-sized companies and acquires established advisory firms, developing them further on one shared base. On top of the systems we buy, we build our own software: a data layer above DATEV, the tools our advisors use every day, and agents that take over recurring work. What counts is daily use, on data that is audited and closed.

As one of our first engineers, you build across the whole stack: data pipelines, backend, the interfaces advisors use and the agents on top. You take a problem from the first conversation with an advisor to software that runs every day. We are hiring our CTO in parallel, who will own the architecture and lead the team. You work directly with Moritz Vogel.

What you'll do

Tools advisors use

  • Sit with tax advisors and accountants on real cases, find where the work gets stuck, and turn it into software they use the next day. Your benchmark: an advisor would miss it if it were switched off.

  • Build interfaces, dashboards and internal tools, from the first prototype to something that runs without you.

  • Ship small and often: a tool in daily use beats a perfect plan.

Data and integration

  • Build the pipelines that move data out of DATEV and our other systems into our own data layer every night, checked from the first day.

  • Define every figure exactly once, so a number means the same thing in every tool and report.

  • Connect the systems each acquired firm brings, so one more firm never means one more integration project.

Agents and automation

  • Build agents that take over recurring work, with a clear line between what the model judges and what is calculated deterministically.

  • Make every result traceable by version, source and decision, so a certified professional can sign off on it.

  • Evaluate against closed, audited cases, not against test data.

Questions you'll answer

  • Which recurring task in an accounting team is the first one worth taking off people's hands, and how do you prove it?

  • How do you build fast now without leaving a mess for the next engineer?

  • When is a prototype ready to run on real data every day, and who signs off before it does?

What success looks like

  • 3 months: Your first tool is in daily use by an advisory team, and the nightly data load runs with checks.

  • 6 months: Several tools and the first agents run in regular operation. You own one area end to end, and others build on your code.

  • 12 months: You own a part of our software with its own users, and new engineers learn from your standards.

Where it leads: from engineer to owning a product area, as a senior engineer or by leading a team, decided by contribution, not by years served.

What you bring

  • A degree in computer science, mathematics, physics, engineering or a related field from a strong university such as TUM, or an equally strong record of your own projects.

  • You have shipped software that other people used, at work, as a working student or in your own project.

  • You write production code in at least one language, ideally Python or TypeScript, and you are at home with SQL and relational databases.

  • AI is your everyday tool: you write, review and test code with it, and you know where it goes wrong.

  • You want breadth across data, backend, interface and agents, and you work in German and in person, because our advisors and clients do.

  • You learn from practitioners, and you set the highest standard in everything you ship, not because someone checks, but because mediocrity bothers you.

A plus, not a requirement

  • One to two years as an engineer in a young startup or scale-up, or a working-student role where you owned something real.

  • Knowledge of accounting, tax or DATEV, or data pipelines and agents you have run in production.

  • No conventional CV required: a mathematician or physicist who builds, an information systems graduate with a real engineering track, or the founder of a small product. We assess contribution, not labels. The range shown is not room for negotiation but a profile scale: the lower end stands for starting right after university, the upper third for someone who already carries the standard work of the role on their own. A different background starts at a different market price and converges on the role's level after twelve months of proven performance.

What this role is and what it isn't

  • Building on a running business, not a greenfield. DATEV runs and clients do not wait. What you build has to work next to daily operations.

  • An operating company, not a software vendor. The users are our own teams. What we build and in which order is decided together with management; you shape how.

  • Breadth, not a specialist track. If you want to perfect one layer for years, this is the wrong role.

Why join us

  • Real data and real users from the first day. Decades of audited, closed work, and advisors who use what you ship the same week.

  • Leverage through acquisitions. Every firm that joins Vogel runs on what you build.

  • Close to the decisions. You work directly with management and see what gets built and why. Hierarchical in decisions, flat in communication, autonomous in execution. Performance is celebrated, not hidden, without politics and without consensus theater.

  • Substance behind you. A profitable, growing business. No funding round decides whether your work continues.

The FAQ below is in German, as is our working day.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub?

Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Dazu Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus – nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt.

Benefits sind bei uns nicht das Sahnehäubchen, sondern das, was Intensität über Jahre tragbar macht: Examensförderung mit 25.000 EUR Qualifizierungsbudget und drei Monaten Freistellung, 100-prozentige Übernahme der Kinderbetreuung, EGYM Wellpass, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Job-Ticket mit 90 % Zuschuss, Homeoffice-Ausstattung und ein Gerät deiner Wahl aus unserem Katalog, ein Buch im Monat aus dem Vogel-Kanon – und KI-Tools ohne Token-Limit und ohne Budgetdeckel. Urlaub: 28 Tage.

title: Founding Legal Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Grubel

Grubel is a research lab that builds AI for high-stakes knowledge work, starting with law. Legal matters require specialized expertise, and each one involves its own facts, practices, parties, and institutions. General-purpose AI applies the same system to every legal matter, varying only what goes into a limited context window.

To meet the depth and diversity of legal work, we let every matter build its own AI: engineer the right data for the matter, adapt the model and agent to it, and track what improves. We combine the three into a matter-specific improvement loop that runs until the system delivers what the matter demands.

Grubel was founded in 2026 by Moritz Hardt, director at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems and formerly a UC Berkeley professor and Google Brain researcher; and Reinhard Heckel, professor of machine learning at the Technical University of Munich, on leave to build Grubel. The founding team includes engineers with PhDs in computer science and experience in foundation-model pretraining at Mistral and legal AI research at Thomson Reuters. The lab has offices in Munich and Tübingen.

Point Nine led an oversubscribed pre-seed funding round with backing from leading AI researchers and founders, including Jeff Dean, Chris Ré, Ion Stoica, and Harvey co-founders Gabe Pereyra and Winston Weinberg.


About the role

You are a skilled lawyer ideally with experience on building legal AI software eager to shape the technological future of your field. As a Founding Legal Engineer, you impact how we scope, build, and evaluate AI systems for complex legal work, and how these systems enter legal practice.

Working directly with Grubel’s founding team, you will shape our research, development, and product: Translate complex legal processes into agentic workflows, evaluate our systems for legal soundness and utility, and work with customers to set our product and engineering standards. You need not write code, but you’re passionate about understanding our technology deeply. Working in a fast-moving team at the intersection of AI research, legal practice, and technology excites you.

What you’ll work on

  • Designing realistic tasks, datasets, and evaluation rubrics for training and evaluation of our legal AI systems

  • Translating complex legal processes into agentic workflows together with our researchers and engineers

  • Evaluating system outputs for legal accuracy, usefulness, and failure modes

  • Leading enterprise pilots and implementations

  • Supporting customer discovery, demonstrations, and go-to-market initiatives

You may be a good fit if

  • You have law degree and strong academic record

  • You have experience practicing law—whether at a law firm, in-house, or in another legal setting

  • You are proactive, self-directed, and comfortable taking broad ownership at an early-stage company

  • You are curious about how AI systems work and comfortable working closely with researchers and engineers

Logistics

  • Munich or Tübingen. We value working together in person, prefer candidates based near one of our offices, and expect at least one day per week in the office. We plan to establish a Zurich office in 2027.

  • Full time employment

  • Competitive salary plus a stock option grant in Grubel, Inc., our US parent company.

title: Functioneel applicatiebeheerder Backend Platform
descriptionHtml:
Bouw jij mee aan betrouwbaar functioneel beheer voor applicaties die onze collega’s dagelijks nodig hebben?

Wie ben jij

Je vindt het leuk om je vast te bijten in applicaties en processen en neemt technische kennis mee. Wanneer een gebruiker met een vraag of probleem komt, wil jij niet alleen weten hoe je het oplost, maar ook begrijpen waar het vandaan komt.

Je beweegt gemakkelijk tussen business en IT. Je kunt met een gebruiker praten over een bedrijfsproces en vervolgens met technische collega's of een leverancier bepalen wat er nodig is om een probleem op te lossen of een verbetering te realiseren.

Daarnaast kijk je verder dan je eigen applicatie. Je begrijpt dat systemen steeds meer met elkaar verbonden zijn en houdt daarom rekening met afhankelijkheden binnen de gehele keten.

We vinden het belangrijk dat je:

  • HBO werk- en denkniveau hebt, bij voorkeur met een relevante opleiding;

  • ervaring hebt met applicatiebeheer of een vergelijkbare functie;

  • affiniteit hebt met bedrijfsprocessen en informatiesystemen;

  • gebruikersvragen en problemen kunt analyseren en vertalen naar effectieve oplossingen;

  • ervaring hebt met het testen en implementeren van wijzigingen;

  • oog hebt voor de samenhang tussen applicaties, processen en IT-ketens;

  • ervaring hebt met Agile werken;

  • initiatief neemt, verantwoordelijkheid pakt en proactief handelt;

  • helder communiceert en gemakkelijk samenwerkt met gebruikers, IT-collega's en leveranciers.

Ervaring met applicaties of processen binnen Finance, Verzekeringen of HR is een pré. Denk bijvoorbeeld aan CODA, Crescendo, QIS of AFAS. Je hoeft ze zeker niet allemaal te kennen. We vinden het vooral belangrijk dat je ervaring hebt met applicatiebeheer en je nieuwe applicaties en bedrijfsprocessen snel eigen kunt maken.

Wat ga je doen

Als Functioneel Applicatiebeheerder ben jij een belangrijke schakel tussen gebruikers, de business, IT-teams en leveranciers. Je zorgt ervoor dat applicaties en IT-diensten betrouwbaar functioneren en dat gebruikers goed worden ondersteund. Je werkt aan zowel de dagelijkse operatie als aan de verdere professionalisering van het beheer. Afhankelijk van jouw kennis, ervaring en de behoefte binnen Backend Platform kun je bijvoorbeeld werken aan applicaties binnen Finance, Verzekeringen of HR.


Je werkzaamheden bestaan onder andere uit:

  • functioneel beheren en ondersteunen van één of meerdere bedrijfskritische applicaties;

  • behandelen en analyseren van functionele vragen, incidenten en verstoringen;

  • bewaken van de goede werking en continuïteit van applicaties;

  • analyseren van gewenste wijzigingen en bepalen wat deze betekenen voor de applicatie en de omliggende keten;

  • afstemmen met gebruikers, leveranciers en IT-collega's over problemen, oplossingen en verbeteringen;

  • ondersteunen bij het realiseren en implementeren van wijzigingen;

  • voorbereiden, coördineren en uitvoeren van functionele en ketentesten;

  • bewaken dat wijzigingen correct en beheerst in gebruik worden genomen;

  • signaleren van mogelijkheden om processen, applicaties en het gebruik daarvan verder te verbeteren;

  • vastleggen en delen van kennis over applicaties, processen en werkwijzen.

Wat bieden wij

Bij Univé IT bieden we je een uitdagende functie binnen een dynamische organisatie, waarin je veel ruimte krijgt om mee te bouwen aan professioneel en toekomstgericht applicatiebeheer.

  • Veel ruimte voor eigen initiatief, eigenaarschap en vakinhoudelijke ontwikkeling.

  • Nauwe samenwerking met ervaren collega’s binnen IT, architectuur, security en waardestromen.

  • De mogelijkheid om actief bij te dragen aan de verdere professionalisering van IT Kern.

  • Ruimte om mee te denken over marktontwikkelingen, automatisering en de inzet van AI binnen Unive en IT.

Arbeidsvoorwaarden

  • Jaarsalaris van € 51.777 tot € 71.907 bruto per jaar op basis van 38 uur, inclusief vakantiegeld en dertiende maand en exclusief variabele beloning;

  • Dienstverband van 32 tot 38 uur per week;

  • Standplaats Zwolle of Assen, met hybride werken in overleg met het team;

  • Variabele collectieve prestatiebeloning van maximaal 9% van het jaarsalaris;

  • 26 vakantiedagen bij een 38-urige werkweek;

  • Goede pensioen- en studiekostenregeling;

  • Thuiswerk- en reiskostenvergoeding;

  • Korting op schade- en zorgverzekeringen bij Univé.

Wie wij zijn

Univé is een coöperatieve organisatie die dicht bij haar leden staat. Als IT-organisatie werken we aan een wendbaar, betrouwbaar, veilig en toekomstgericht IT-landschap. Schaalbare technologie, goede processen, standaardisatie en continu verbeteren zijn daarbij belangrijk. Binnen IT Kern werken verschillende teams aan het beheren, ondersteunen en doorontwikkelen van applicaties, platformen, infrastructuur, netwerkdiensten en securityoplossingen. Deze IT-diensten zijn essentieel voor onze dagelijkse dienstverlening aan leden en voor de ondersteuning van onze collega’s. Samen bouwen we aan een moderne IT-organisatie waarin we betrouwbaar functioneren, waardestromen goed worden ondersteund en vernieuwing gecontroleerd en toekomstbestendig kan plaatsvinden. Je komt terecht in een team waarin samenwerking, eigenaarschap en plezier in het werk belangrijk zijn. We werken met collega’s die graag verbeteren, verantwoordelijkheid nemen en elkaar helpen om het applicatie- en IT-landschap iedere dag een stukje beter te maken.

title: Growth Account Executive, EMEA
descriptionHtml:
About Telnyx

Telnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it. From architecting and amplifying the reach of a private, global, multi-cloud IP network, to bringing hyperlocal edge technology right to your fingertips through intuitive APIs, we're shaping a new era of seamless interconnection between people, devices, and applications.

We're driven by a desire to transform and modernize what's antiquated, automate the manual, and solve real-world problems through innovative connectivity solutions. As a testament to our success, we're proud to stand as a financially stable and profitable company. Our robust profitability allows us not only to invest in pioneering technologies but also to foster an environment of continuous learning and growth for our team.

Our collective vision is a world where borderless connectivity fuels limitless innovation. By joining us, you can be part of laying the foundations for this interconnected future. We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers.

The Role

Most sales roles chase new logos. This one unlocks the revenue already inside Telnyx's customer base — and there's a lot of it.

As a Growth Account Executive (Expansion), you'll take commercial ownership of established Telnyx customers after their first 12 months, identifying and closing new revenue opportunities across our product portfolio, from Voice AI and programmable communications to messaging, connectivity, and AI infrastructure.

You'll own an assigned portfolio of existing customers, identify untapped opportunities, build relationships with new stakeholders, and drive expansion from prospecting through close.

This isn't traditional account management. You're not here to simply maintain relationships or renew contracts. You're here to grow accounts by introducing new products, expanding into new business units and geographies, and helping customers build more with Telnyx.

You're not farming. You're hunting inside the base.

What You'll Do

  • Own and grow your accounts. Take commercial ownership of an assigned portfolio of established customers, developing strategies to drive incremental recurring revenue.
  • Find untapped opportunities. Analyze customer usage, product adoption, business models, and growth plans to identify opportunities for cross-selling, upselling, and geographic expansion.
  • Hunt within existing accounts. Run targeted, personalized outbound campaigns to engage new stakeholders, departments, and decision-makers within your customer portfolio.
  • Own the expansion sales cycle. Lead discovery, qualify opportunities, develop commercial proposals, negotiate terms, and close expansion deals.
  • Sell across the Telnyx product portfolio. Identify opportunities spanning Voice AI, SIP trunking, programmable voice, messaging, WhatsApp Business, global numbers, wireless, and AI infrastructure.
  • Build strategic relationships. Develop connections with technical buyers, business leaders, and economic decision-makers to uncover new use cases and accelerate adoption.
  • Drive measurable revenue growth. Own an incremental MRR target, focusing on commercially attributable, profitable expansion rather than organic usage growth alone.
  • Collaborate across teams. Work closely with Hunter AEs during account transitions and partner with Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, and Product teams to execute expansion strategies.
  • Own your forecast. Maintain accurate opportunities, account plans, and forecasts in Salesforce, ensuring clear visibility into pipeline health and commercial progress.
  • Bring customer intelligence back to Telnyx. Share market insights, product feedback, and emerging customer requirements to help shape our roadmap and go-to-market strategy.

What You Bring

  • Experience in B2B technology sales, ideally as an Account Executive, Growth AE, or in a commercially focused business development role.
  • A demonstrated ability to generate pipeline through proactive outbound prospecting rather than relying exclusively on inbound demand.
  • A hunter mentality and the commercial curiosity to identify opportunities that aren't immediately obvious.
  • Strong discovery and consultative selling skills, with the ability to connect technical capabilities to measurable business outcomes.
  • Experience navigating multiple stakeholders and building relationships with both technical and commercial decision-makers.
  • The ability to independently manage opportunities, develop business cases, and move deals through a structured sales process.
  • Strong account research and strategic thinking skills, including identifying whitespace and opportunities for cross-selling.
  • Comfort discussing technical products with developers, engineering teams, operations leaders, and executives.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience managing pipeline and forecasts.
  • A proactive, accountable mindset with a genuine desire to own and deliver revenue results.

Bonus Points

  • Experience in CPaaS, UCaaS, telecom, cloud infrastructure, AI, or developer-focused technology platforms.
  • Familiarity with Voice AI, SIP trunking, programmable communications, WhatsApp Business API, or messaging infrastructure.
  • Previous success in an expansion, cross-sell, upsell, or account-growth role.
  • Experience selling multiple products or solutions into the same organization.
  • Familiarity with MEDDPICC or another structured qualification methodology.
  • Experience working with international or multinational customers across Europe.

Why This Role Matters

Telnyx customers are already building on our infrastructure, but many are only using a fraction of what our platform can offer.

A customer using us for SIP trunking might be a strong fit for Voice AI. A business operating in one country might be ready to expand across Europe. These opportunities don't always arrive as inbound requests. Someone needs to uncover them, build the business case, and turn them into revenue.

That's where you come in. You'll work on a warm base with real relationships, real usage data, and real expansion potential. The upside is there. You just have to go and find it.

You'll be measured on the incremental revenue you create, not simply the accounts you inherit.

Why Telnyx

  • Real technology, built in-house. We own our global network and build our communications and AI infrastructure, giving you a differentiated platform to sell.
  • A broad portfolio with real cross-sell potential. From global connectivity and programmable communications to Voice AI and AI infrastructure, there's always another customer challenge we can solve.
  • Profitable and independent. Join a company focused on sustainable growth and long-term investment in its technology.

title: Growth & Marketing Manager (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Jobbeschreibung

Warum gibt es diese Rolle - und warum jetzt?

Lovebetter wächst in eine neue Phase. Wir haben eine klare Mission, starke Inhalte, eine etablierte Marke und zahlreiche Möglichkeiten, noch mehr Männer zu erreichen und nachhaltig zu wachsen.

In den vergangenen Jahren haben wir unterschiedliche Marketingkanäle aufgebaut, Partnerschaften entwickelt und wertvolle Erfahrungen gesammelt. Jetzt wollen wir diese Aktivitäten noch besser miteinander verbinden, neue Wachstumschancen erschließen und unsere Ideen schneller in die Umsetzung bringen.

Dafür suchen wir dich.

Als Growth & Marketing Manager bist du eine zentrale operative Kraft in unserem Marketing. Du verbindest kreatives Denken mit analytischem Verständnis, entwickelst eigene Ideen und sorgst dafür, dass aus Konzepten konkrete Kampagnen, Tests und Ergebnisse werden.

Diese Rolle ist bewusst breiter als ein klassischer Marketingjob. Du wirst nicht nur einen einzelnen Kanal betreuen, sondern in ganz unterschiedlichen Bereichen mitarbeiten, eigenständig Verantwortung übernehmen und neue Themen vorantreiben.

Du musst dafür nicht alles bereits können. Entscheidend ist, dass du neugierig bist, schnell lernst, lösungsorientiert denkst und Lust hast, Dinge selbst in die Hand zu nehmen.

Wofür Lovebetter steht

Wir lösen sexuelle Probleme wie vorzeitigen Samenerguss oder Erektionsprobleme mit Männern und befähigen sie, ihre innere Stärke, sexuelle Zufriedenheit und Lebensqualität von innen heraus zu transformieren.

Unsere Arbeit wirkt weit über den Einzelnen hinaus: auf Partnerschaften, Familien und kommende Generationen.

Wir suchen jemanden, der unsere Mission mitgestalten möchte, Verantwortung übernimmt und versteht, dass wirkungsvolles Marketing Kreativität, analytisches Denken und konsequente Umsetzung verbindet.

Deine Mission als Growth & Marketing Manager

Du machst Lovebetters Marketing vielseitiger, effizienter und wachstumsstärker.

Du entwickelst Marketingideen, setzt Kampagnen um, betreust bestehende und neue Wachstumskanäle und erkennst anhand von Daten, was funktioniert und wo wir besser werden können.

Dabei arbeitest du eng mit unserem CMO, unseren Content-Produzenten, Agenturen und externen Partnern zusammen.

Du übernimmst eigenständig Projekte – von der ersten Idee über die operative Umsetzung bis zur anschließenden Auswertung. Dabei bewegst du dich selbstverständlich zwischen kreativen, analytischen und organisatorischen Aufgaben.

Besonders wichtig: Du wartest nicht darauf, dass dir jemand für jede Herausforderung eine Lösung vorgibt. Du recherchierst, probierst aus, eignest dir neue Fähigkeiten an und findest Wege, Dinge umzusetzen.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Marketingkampagnen entwickeln und umsetzen: Du planst und realisierst kanalübergreifende Marketingmaßnahmen, entwickelst kreative Ansätze und begleitest Kampagnen von der Idee bis zur Erfolgsauswertung.
  • Neue Wachstumskanäle erschließen: Du identifizierst neue Möglichkeiten, unsere Zielgruppe zu erreichen, recherchierst Potenziale, entwickelst erste Tests und hilfst dabei, erfolgreiche Ansätze systematisch auszubauen.
  • Ambassador Marketing und Kooperationen vorantreiben: Du entwickelst unser Ambassador-Programm weiter, recherchierst und gewinnst passende Partner, betreust Kooperationen und sorgst dafür, dass aus Beziehungen messbare Marketingmaßnahmen entstehen.
  • Content und Creatives mitgestalten: Du entwickelst Themen, Hooks, Texte und Kampagnenideen, erstellst Briefings und arbeitest mit unseren Content-Produzenten an Inhalten für unterschiedliche Plattformen und Marketingkanäle.
  • CRM und E-Mail-Marketing betreuen: Du setzt Newsletter und Kampagnen um, entwickelst Segmentierungs- und Reaktivierungsansätze und unterstützt dabei, bestehende Kontakte gezielter anzusprechen.
  • Marketingperformance analysieren und optimieren: Du behältst relevante KPIs im Blick, analysierst Kampagnen, Content und Funnels, erkennst Verbesserungspotenziale und leitest konkrete Maßnahmen daraus ab.
  • Websites und Landingpages weiterentwickeln: Du übernimmst kleinere Anpassungen an unseren digitalen Angeboten und unterstützt bei Tests und Optimierungen. Wenn du dafür ein neues Tool wie WordPress lernen musst, arbeitest du dich eigenständig ein.
  • Marketingprojekte und Partner koordinieren: Du hältst laufende Projekte zusammen, koordinierst interne und externe Beteiligte und sorgst dafür, dass Aufgaben zuverlässig und termingerecht umgesetzt werden.
  • KI und Automatisierung sinnvoll einsetzen: Du nutzt moderne KI-Tools für Recherche, Content, Analysen und operative Aufgaben und entwickelst Ideen, wie wir unsere Marketingprozesse kontinuierlich verbessern können.

Was diese Rolle besonders macht

  • Abwechslung statt Silodenken: Du arbeitest nicht ausschließlich an Content, Performance oder Analytics, sondern lernst unterschiedliche Marketingdisziplinen kennen und verbindest sie miteinander.
  • Eigenverantwortung statt langer Abstimmungswege: Du bekommst Raum, eigene Ideen einzubringen, Entscheidungen vorzubereiten und Projekte selbstständig voranzutreiben.
  • Kreativität trifft Zahlen: Du kannst neue Kampagnenideen entwickeln und anschließend anhand konkreter Ergebnisse nachvollziehen, ob sie erfolgreich waren.
  • Lernen gehört zum Job: Du musst nicht jedes Tool und jeden Marketingkanal bereits kennen. Wir schätzen Menschen, die sich Herausforderungen stellen und neue Fähigkeiten selbstständig aufbauen.
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit dem CMO: Du erhältst Einblicke in strategische Marketingentscheidungen und bist eng an der Weiterentwicklung unseres Marketings beteiligt.
  • Persönliche Entwicklung und Perspektive: Du wächst mit deinen Aufgaben und hast die Möglichkeit, mit der Weiterentwicklung von Lovebetter zunehmend Verantwortung für größere Projekte, Prozesse und perspektivisch auch Menschen zu übernehmen.

Dein Impact

Wenn du deinen Job exzellent machst, entsteht:

  • ein Marketing, in dem gute Ideen schneller in konkrete Maßnahmen umgesetzt werden
  • ein Ambassador- und Kooperationsprogramm, das kontinuierlich wächst und messbare Ergebnisse liefert
  • neue Marketingkanäle, die strukturiert getestet, bewertet und weiterentwickelt werden
  • bessere Kampagnen und Inhalte durch die Verbindung von Kreativität und datenbasierten Erkenntnissen
  • optimierte Funnels, CRM-Kampagnen und digitale Kontaktpunkte, die mehr qualifizierte Leads erzeugen
  • effizientere Prozesse durch Eigeninitiative, Automatisierung und den sinnvollen Einsatz von KI
  • ein Marketing-Team, das schneller, selbstständiger und wirkungsvoller arbeitet

Klingt nach dir?

Dann freuen wir uns, dich kennenzulernen.

Schick uns keine Standardbewerbung.

Erzähl uns lieber:

  • welche Marketingprojekte oder Kampagnen du bereits eigenständig umgesetzt hast
  • wann du dich zuletzt in ein völlig neues Thema oder Tool eingearbeitet hast und was daraus entstanden ist
  • wie du kreative Ideen entwickelst und herausfindest, ob sie tatsächlich funktionieren
  • welche Aufgaben du schon übernommen hast, obwohl du sie vorher noch nie gemacht hattest
  • und warum du glaubst, dass genau du Lovebetters Marketing mit Kreativität, Eigeninitiative und Umsetzungskraft auf das nächste Level bringen kannst

Stellenanforderungen

Wen wir suchen (und wen nicht)

Diese Rolle passt zu dir, wenn …

  • du bereits praktische Erfahrung im digitalen Marketing gesammelt und idealerweise Kampagnen oder Projekte eigenständig umgesetzt hast
  • du sowohl kreativ als auch analytisch denkst und Spaß daran hast, zwischen unterschiedlichen Aufgaben zu wechseln
  • du eine ausgeprägte Hands-on-Mentalität mitbringst und lieber ins Machen kommst, als lange über Möglichkeiten zu diskutieren
  • du neugierig bist, schnell lernst und dir neue Tools, Plattformen oder Fähigkeiten eigenständig aneignen kannst
  • du auch vor unbekannten Herausforderungen nicht zurückschreckst und den Mut hast, Neues auszuprobieren
  • du Marketingkennzahlen verstehst und aus Ergebnissen sinnvolle Schlussfolgerungen ziehen kannst
  • du strukturiert und zuverlässig arbeitest, Prioritäten setzen kannst und auch bei mehreren parallelen Projekten den Überblick behältst
  • du KI bereits aktiv nutzt oder motiviert bist, sie schnell und sinnvoll in deinen Arbeitsalltag zu integrieren
  • du sehr gut auf Deutsch kommunizierst und ein Gespür für überzeugende Texte und zielgruppengerechte Ansprache hast
  • du Verantwortung übernehmen möchtest und Lust hast, gemeinsam mit uns zu wachsen

Diese Rolle ist nichts für dich, wenn …

  • du ausschließlich in einer einzelnen Marketingdisziplin arbeiten möchtest und wenig Interesse an anderen Bereichen hast
  • du für neue Aufgaben immer eine detaillierte Schritt-für-Schritt-Anleitung brauchst

Why Hawk-Eye & Why Growth Sports❓

This exciting opportunity to join our passionate and enthusiastic team will take you to elite-level sporting events all around the world. As a member of our team, you will be responsible for delivering Hawk-Eye technology across a diverse range of current sports, including Athletics, Gaelic Sports, Volleyball, Horse Racing and Motorsports. You would be coming into a Badminton Operator role as presently, Badminton makes up the large majority of our global deployments, but our landscape can shift quickly. The 'Growth' in Growth Sports is literal: we are a highly agile department built for rapid expansion, significant pivots, and the continuous pursuit of new sporting opportunities. You will play a crucial role in maintaining excellence in our current sports, while helping us deliver innovative solutions to an ever-expanding roster of new clients.

The Growth Sports department delivers our Tracking and Replay products across a wide range of sporting applications, both in the UK and globally. We are always growing and developing new cutting-edge services for our clients, and with this expansion comes the need for new faces to join our team and help drive our ongoing innovation.

Successful applicants will receive training on the basic skills and knowledge required to be a Hawk-Eye operator - and then it’s time to get to an event and get immediately hands-on with our technology! We pride ourselves on supporting the development of our people, and we look forward to challenging you in a job that is truly unique.

What Does A Typical Day Look Like?🛠

  • Pre-Match & Tournament Preparations: Liaise with key stakeholders such as broadcast personnel, match officials and other teams to ensure all contractual obligations are seamlessly delivered;

  • Technology Setup: Set up our cutting-edge Tracking and SMART Replay technologies at venues around the world;

  • System Checks: Conduct thorough pre-match system checks to ensure everything runs efficiently;

  • Match-Day Operations: Monitoring and operating Hawk-Eye technologies during matches;

  • Performance Monitoring: Keep a close eye on hardware and software, troubleshooting any issues that arise;

  • Agile Deployment & Cross-Training: Adapt quickly to operational changes, applying your technical knowledge to new sports and systems as the department expands and pivots;

  • Post-Match Reporting: Complete detailed reports to enhance future operations and client satisfaction;

  • Off-Season Maintenance & Development: Build and maintain our hardware and equipment, and aid with research and development into new projects and technologies.

Why Is This The Right Job For You? ✅

  • Passion & Innovation: Passionate about sport in general with a desire to innovate.

  • Technical Proficiency: A strong foundation in technology with a desire to problem-solve.

  • Agility & Adaptability: Highly resilient to change. You thrive in a dynamic environment where the primary focus can pivot rapidly from one sport to another as the business scales.

  • Proactive Attitude: Ability to take initiative with a willingness to learn as much as possible.

  • Time Management: Excellent time management skills to thrive in a live broadcast environment.

  • Communication: Professional and approachable, with strong listening skills under pressure.

  • Flexibility: Willingness to travel domestically and overseas and to work weekends.

At Hawk-Eye Innovations, we appreciate and value the importance of potential and growth. If you believe that you excel in certain areas and possess the passion and desire to develop further, we encourage you to apply.

What Difficulties Might I Face?🔦

Up to this point, I’m sure there have been many things that you find intriguing about the role, however, it is not without its unique challenges. Here are some that you can expect to find with the role:

Dynamic & Changing Scope: Because our department is built for growth, our primary focus can shift rapidly. You must be comfortable with the unpredictability of scaling up new sports at short notice and stepping outside your comfort zone.

Working Hours: Due to the nature of the sports industry, there is often work on weekends and midweek evenings and we are expected to fulfil our roles until the last kick.

Travelling Abroad: You can expect to spend periods of the year working throughout Europe and internationally based on the events in the sporting calendar.

High-Pressure Situations: Working in a live broadcast environment on a production that is distributed globally and widely seen by many will bring levels of pressure.

All of these different factors offer different challenges daily as an operator. We will do everything we can to train you and support you to the best possible level but these factors should be considered before submitting your application.

Application & Hiring Process⏳

  • Application: If you're interested in this position, please submit your CV and complete the application form and hit submit.

  • Task Submission: Successful candidates from the application stage will receive invites to access our assessment system. We will ask you to complete a one-way video interview.

  • Review Period: Once you have completed the task, our team will take a period of time to review it and provide application updates.

  • Assessment Event: Successful candidates from the video interview will be invited to one of our Hawk-Eye Assessment Events.

  • Offers & Feedback: The team will take time to review all feedback and conduct our final reviews. All candidates will receive detailed feedback from the assessment event whether they have been successful or not as we appreciate each candidate's desire for development.

We look forward to receiving your application and exploring how you can contribute to the future of sports entertainment at Sony Sports.

title: GTM
descriptionHtml:
Deducta

GTM

Location: London, UK, near London Bridge. Hybrid, 3-4 in-person days a week.

Compensation: From £120k base salary plus equity and commission (£200k+ Realistic OTE)

Visa Sponsorship: Available for the right candidate

Start Date: As soon as possible

Why we exist

Every decision a business makes, from the suppliers it trusts to the risks it accepts, eventually shows up as spend. This makes spend data the most honest record of how a company operates. Not the strategy deck or the org chart: spend describes what really happened.

This record exists, but it's scattered across dozens of systems and decades of legacy technology. Companies spending billions a year still can't easily answer: Who are our suppliers? Where are we exposed? What are we paying for twice?

We believe a business that can't see itself clearly can't make great decisions. Deducta exists to give the world's most complex organisations a true picture of how they operate, and the intelligence to act on it. Our ambition is to become the category-defining platform for enterprise data intelligence.

We're well funded, growing fast, and have already processed more than £1 trillion of spend for some of the world's largest and most recognisable companies. Our partners use Deducta to deliver major business transformations orders of magnitude faster.

Why this role matters

Our partners use Deducta to deliver major transformations, and winning them takes a consultative sale with senior executives. This role owns customer acquisition end to end, from opening relationships with C-suite and VP-level leaders to signed partnership. You'll report to the leadership team.

You'll have significant autonomy to lead sophisticated enterprise deals, work directly with client data in our platform, and build the business cases that win them. You'll carry a quota and be accountable for closing new business. As the commercial function grows, you'll be a leader in it, setting the standard for how we sell and shaping the repeatable motion behind it.

What you'll do

  • Customer acquisition: Own the full sales cycle, from identifying and engaging senior executives through to close.

  • Pipeline generation: Map target accounts, open relationships with senior stakeholders and build a pipeline of enterprises where Deducta can deliver outsized value.

  • Business cases: Build quantified business cases and materials that translate Deducta's capabilities into the outcomes decision-makers care about.

  • Complex deals: Lead multi-stakeholder deals, run product demonstrations, work with client data in the platform, and coordinate product, engineering and delivery to keep momentum.

  • Pipeline discipline: Make next steps, risks, decision-makers and deal status explicit across every opportunity.

  • Closing: Carry a quota and close new enterprise business, negotiating commercial terms and guiding deals through procurement and legal to signature.

Success in this role means:

  • Quota attainment: You consistently hit your number by creating and closing high-quality enterprise opportunities where Deducta can deliver meaningful value.

  • Deal momentum: Complex deals move forward with clear next steps, strong executive sponsorship and fewer stalls or surprises.

  • Trusted before signing: Prospects understand the business case for Deducta and see us as a credible partner before they sign.

  • Repeatable motion: You help make the commercial motion more repeatable, and others learn from how you sell.

Who you are

We're looking for a commercially minded, high-agency seller with a proven track record of closing complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise deals. You'll combine structured problem solving and analytical depth with the drive to win sophisticated enterprise customers.

You might be the right fit if you have:

  • Executive presence: You can sit across from a CPO or CFO, earn their trust and build a relationship that lasts beyond the deal.

  • Commercial judgement: You read an account, understand what matters to each stakeholder and find the best path to a decision.

  • Analytical instincts: You work directly with client data and turn the analysis into a clear, compelling business case.

  • Programme management: You coordinate complex, multi-stakeholder processes and follow through without a pre-existing playbook.

  • Product fluency: You run product demonstrations and work in the platform yourself rather than relying on others.

  • Drive to win: You have the hunger to create opportunities, sustain momentum and close business, with a record of hitting or exceeding quota.

  • Nice to have: Entrepreneurial experience, experience mentoring or leading others, or prior startup or high-growth go-to-market experience.

We care most about how you think, the quality of your work and how you approach unfamiliar problems. Previous startup experience isn't essential, but the pace, initiative and judgement to thrive in one are.

How we work

We believe in freedom and responsibility. We set clear priorities, share the context and trust people to decide how to deliver. You'll thrive here if you value:

  • Ownership: You own the outcome, not just the task. You deliver what you commit to, follow through when things get difficult, and own your mistakes.

  • Unreasonable hospitality: You treat prospects, clients and teammates with exceptional care as a default. You anticipate needs, communicate with clarity, and help others succeed.

  • Bias for action: We don’t have every answer upfront. You move things forward without waiting to be asked, take calculated risks, and adapt as you learn.

  • Craft: Moving quickly matters, but so does doing work that stays clear, reliable and useful as we grow.

  • System building: You create leverage beyond your own output, building processes, tools and documentation that others reuse and that keep working without you.

  • Candor: You tell the hard truth early, give and receive feedback thoughtfully, ask for help when you need it, and push back when priorities need to change.

  • Curiosity about AI: You’re excited by what applied AI makes possible, and you look for ways to use it in your own work.

As an early team member, you'll help shape our culture, our processes and where Deducta goes next. We're growing quickly, and this role will grow with us.

Hiring process

  1. Intro call

  2. Background interview

  3. Technical exercise

  4. Final interview

  5. Offer, referencing and start

Help the world's biggest businesses finally see themselves clearly.

title: Hardware Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

The BMS is where software meets power. As our Hardware Engineer, you'll own the hardware side of the Anori BMS with a focus on the power stage: power electronics, cell connection and protection circuits. At the same time, you'll be our go-to person for hardware testing and make sure every board holds up under real-world conditions, from HiL test benches to stress tests and EMC pre-compliance. You'll work closely with Stefan, our CTO, and our firmware engineers to take the BMS from a tested prototype to a fully certified product. The technology is proven, the funding is secured, and the hardware decisions you make now will define how every future Anori BMS works.

Start date: from January 1, 2027

What You'll Do

  • Design and develop the power stage of our BMS: the highest power density on the market

  • Make the trade-off between performance, reliability, supply chain and price for each part

  • Build and run hardware tests: HiL setups, stress tests, HALTs and failure analysis

  • Plan and run EMC pre-compliance testing and prepare the path to conformity

  • Bring up new boards and debug them together with the firmware team

  • Contribute across the entire BMS hardware, wherever you are needed

What You Bring

Must have

  • Solid foundation in electrical engineering, from the schematic to the PCB. You know the parasitic effects of every practical circuit and you design with them

  • Deep knowledge of power electronics: MOSFET switch design, SOA, gate drive, current sensing and loss budgets

  • Experience with protection circuits, e.g. overcurrent, short circuit, over- and undervoltage, reverse polarity

  • Circuit and thermal simulation, for example in LTspice, with model-to-hardware correlation on the bench

  • Confident in the lab: oscilloscopes, power supplies, electronic loads, thermal measurements and of course hand-soldering 01005 components

  • Critical, analytical, systematic thinking: you reason from first principles, make your assumptions explicit and challenge existing paradigms

Strongly preferred

  • A broad hardware skill set beyond the power stage: microcontroller circuits, analog sensing, communication interfaces (CAN, LIN, BLE, …)

  • Proven hands-on testing experience, including HiL tests and stress tests

  • Knowledge of DfM and new electronic manufacturing techniques, materials and general mechanical integration knowledge

  • Thermal design and cooling concepts for high-current paths

  • Wide-bandgap semiconductors and new switch topologies, and an interest to research and develop novel gate-drive techniques beyond standard drivers

Nice to have

  • High-voltage design above 60V: creepage and clearance, isolation, isolation monitoring and safe discharge

  • Experience with battery systems, cell connection and cell monitoring ICs (AFEs)

  • Test automation with Python

  • A background in safety-critical systems (IEC 61508, ISO 26262, …)

  • Knowledge in MBSE and requirements engineering methods (the skills, not the paper)

You don't tick every box? Apply anyway. No one matches a job description 100%. If this role excites you and you see yourself growing into it, we want to hear from you.

What We Offer

  • Work on a product with purpose that redefines the state of art: our product is a key part to enable competitive battery energy storage.

  • Work directly with the founding team on decisions that shape the company. The team is small, so your ideas will matter. A lot.

  • Challenging engineering in an industrial, but research-near environment. We bring research into the industry.

  • A modern stack and methods: Rust, MBSE, everything as code, and the best tools and techniques for the job, chosen on merit.

  • To be both supported and challenged: room to grow, and the expectation that you will.

You might be a fit if

  • You hold yourself to a high standard and don’t settle for "good enough."

  • You want to have a big say in what the Anori BMS looks like and how it works

  • You are eager to try out new tools and enjoy incorporating AI into your work to make your life easier and more productive

  • You are excited about startups and all the opportunities and uncertainties that come with it

  • You want to be an active part in accelerating the energy transition in Europe

  • You are comfortable with English as a working language

  • You are happy to be in the office most of the time because for fast decisions we need to be in the same room. We expect you to be in the office at least 3 days / week

You also want to become an Anori? We cannot wait to meet you. Go and click the apply button. Don’t be shy, we are nice.

P.S. Extra bonus if you tell us what your favorite type of tea is.

title: Head of Applied AI
descriptionHtml:
Head of Applied AI

Location: Our offices are in Central London, along with several of our customers. Travel to our customer sites is required, the frequency of which will vary from customer-to-customer. You need to be able to travel onsite to London up to 3 days per week, although onsite requirements will vary week-to-week and customer-to-customer from 0 to 3 days.

Defence/SC Clearance Requirements:

SC clearance is required for our customer facing teams. You do not need active SC clearance as we will undertake checks upon you joining, but you must be eligible to pass SC clearance. DV clearance may be required for certain roles, so the ability/willingness to pass DV clearance is advantageous but not essential.

About Cloudscaler

Cloudscaler is a rapidly growing cloud consultancy. We partner with ambitious enterprise and public sector customers to design, build, operate, and support secure, governed cloud platforms that meet the highest regulatory and industry standards.

We are scaling deliberately. Our revenue ambition depends on deploying the right people onto the right work quickly, and on making disciplined use of our capacity. This role is central to that.

 

About the role

Cloudscaler's Applied AI business unit launched at the start of 2026 and has grown quickly, with an established offering, live client engagements and a pipeline in place. The current Head of Applied AI is stepping back from the role for personal reasons and remains with the business to hand over, so the incoming Head inherits a running unit rather than a standing start. We are recruiting to take it into its next phase of growth.

The work is running; the structure is not yet. Offerings are defined, collateral exists, engagements are live and Cloudscaler's public voice on applied AI is established. What does not yet exist is the shape around it: there is no ring-fenced team, no separate P&L and no formally defined roles. The unit began with strategy, technical expertise and sales all held in one place. Technical capability has grown since; strategy and commercial ownership have not. Formalising the practice - defining the team, the roles and the commercial structure - is part of the job rather than something the incoming Head inherits finished.

This role has both external and internal responsibilities:

Externally, it owns our AI go-to-market offerings and the customer, partner and pre-sales activity that turns them into pipeline, and it is Cloudscaler's public voice on applied AI.

Internally, it carries full commercial accountability for the business unit, provides technical delivery oversight, builds and leads the practice, and is accountable for enabling the whole company to work with AI.

The role reports to the CTO and works closely with leadership across the business. The person needs to be technical enough to direct and challenge the engineering work, and commercially credible enough to scale the unit and its offering.

It is a hands-on role. In one week, you might write a business case for the Leadership Team, advise a client CTO on their AI strategy, review an engineer's architecture decision and speak at a conference on what we have learned.

External responsibilities

These responsibilities are customer-facing, partner-facing and public facing:

Relentless client focus - Maintaining a relentless client focus, calibrated to how mature the business unit is, and being decisive about where to concentrate effort and what to stop. Early on that means client meetings and pipeline growth; later it means shifting weight to larger, more sustainable areas of demand.

AI go-to-market offerings - Defining and owning our AI go-to-market offerings, working with sales to take them to market. For each offering, defining what it is, who buys it, the problem it solves, its indicative price and its delivery model, and reviewing the set as the market moves, retiring what no longer sells and evolving what does.

Customer relationships - Building trusted-advisor relationships with our customers, from CTOs and CDOs to engineering leaders, advising at every level and translating the same insight into the right language for a C-suite sponsor setting strategy and for the developers implementing it. Converting those relationships into repeat work and referenceable engagements.

Pre-sales leadership - Leading pre-sales activity on AI opportunities, from qualification through to proposal. Supporting the delivery and commercial teams on proposals, workshops and pitches, and leading on bids where applied AI credibility is the differentiator. Qualifying opportunities in or out, including declining those we should not pursue.

Client collateral - Developing reusable client collateral (opportunity assessments, roadmaps and business cases) grounded in real delivery experience. Keeping it current as the offerings and the technology move and making it available to the delivery and commercial teams rather than rebuilt for each deal.

Partner and industry relationships - Building and owning our AI partner and industry relationships (AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI and relevant industry bodies), including the technical relationship, joint go-to-market activity, and achieving and maintaining the respective AI partner competencies that matter to our customers. An existing network inside our partners is a significant advantage, as is fluency in how each organisation works, where it sits in the market and what it is seeking to achieve commercially. Deciding which competencies to pursue and in what order and keeping them current.

Thought leadership and public voice - Providing thought leadership on applied AI and establishing Cloudscaler's public voice through speaking, meetups, blogs and whitepapers. Building our standing in external applied AI communities and contributing to industry discussion, with material grounded in work we have delivered.

Market awareness - Tracking the AI market as it moves - model releases, tooling and emerging frameworks - and forming a clear view on what is credible, what is hype, and what Cloudscaler should adopt. Bringing that view to the Leadership Team early enough to act on it, and setting our position on what we adopt, what we monitor and what we set aside.

Internal responsibilities

These responsibilities cover the commercial, delivery and capability side of the business unit.

Commercial accountability - Carrying full commercial accountability for the business unit, which is run as its own business and measured on clear financial metrics: pipeline, revenue and gross profit. In the first six months that means a six-month revenue plan, with forecast gross profit covering the cost of the leader within six months and the team gross profit positive within two quarters. This grows into full P&L ownership as the unit scales, including team economics that stand on their own.

Reporting and investment cases - Reporting to the Leadership Team on monthly KPIs covering pipeline, utilisation and gross profit against the six-month plan, and building the investment cases that fund the unit's growth. Reporting runs from month one, including the business case for establishing a dedicated team.

Technical delivery oversight - Providing technical delivery oversight of AI customer engagements, working with our delivery teams. This is an architect's role rather than an engineer's: technical enough to hold your own with client engineers and to delegate the detail, and disciplined enough not to commit to capabilities we cannot feasibly deliver. Reviewing architecture and design decisions and acting as the decision-maker when a technical call is needed.

Building and leading the practice - Building and leading our AI practice: owning Cloudscaler's AI strategy and the roadmap to deliver it, hiring and line-managing the team as it grows, capability development, and a repeatable methodology and delivery standards that make quality consistent regardless of who is leading the engagement. Defining the capability model and establishing the practice as an internal centre of excellence for review and quality assurance as it grows.

Decomposing and delegating ownership - Breaking broad areas of activity into distinct responsibilities that can be delegated and genuinely owned, and building the team to hold them. The scope of this role is deliberately broader than one person can carry: the expectation is that the Head of Applied AI grows a team around them - including the AI enablement hires already in train - and leads through that team rather than delivering everything personally. Internal AI usage guidance, reviewing internal projects, pre-sales attendance, marketing campaigns and enablement workshops each need a named owner; an informal approach works while the unit is small but will not scale.

Accelerators and intellectual property - Building reusable AI accelerators and intellectual property that shorten and de-risk customer delivery. Registering the assets as the work matures - accelerators, frameworks and reference architectures - and working with engineering to keep them testable and current as models and tooling evolve. Treating them as Cloudscaler intellectual property with standalone value rather than delivery tools alone.

Company-wide AI enablement - Enabling every Cloudscaler employee to work with AI, including defining our internal AI learning pathways. Setting the guidance for how AI is used in our own work and running the enablement activity that puts it into everyday use across the whole company rather than the practice alone.

Internal community of practice - Growing an internal AI community of practice, giving colleagues outside the team a route to learn and contribute. Running it as a standing forum rather than ad-hoc sessions, so that colleagues outside the practice can build AI capability alongside their own work.

Candidate profile

This is a senior role combining technical depth with commercial ownership. We expect candidates to demonstrate the following:

Technical depth in applied AI - Current, hands-on understanding of AI technologies, models and tooling, sufficient to direct development work, review architecture and design decisions, and hold credible technical conversations with client engineers and architects.

Commercial track record - Experience owning a revenue or gross profit target, building the pipeline behind it, and reporting against a plan. Comfortable being measured on financial outcomes rather than activity.

Consulting and client credibility - A strong communicator who can advise at C-suite level and at engineering level, and whom clients want in the room on their most significant decisions.

Practice or capability building - Experience building a team or capability from a small base: hiring, setting delivery standards, and creating repeatable methodology rather than relying on individual heroics.

Partner ecosystem experience - Familiarity with the AWS and Anthropic ecosystems, or a comparable hyperscaler and model-vendor landscape, including how partner competencies and joint go-to-market activity work in practice.

External profile - A track record of public contribution on applied AI, or the clear appetite and ability to build one.

Leadership and delegation - Experience leading and line-managing a technical team, including setting direction, delegating genuine ownership and developing people. Comfortable achieving outcomes through a team rather than personally delivering the work.

Judgement and prioritisation - The ability to decide where to concentrate a small team's effort, and the discipline to stop work that is not producing.

Benefits

  • Discretionary bonus

  • Discretionary security clearance bonus for those holding certain clearance

  • Periodic offer of share options schemes

  • 25 days’ annual leave

  • 5 additional days per year towards training, certifications, or charity work

  • Option to buy additional annual leave up to 5 days per year

  • Public holidays opt-out scheme, the option to work on public holidays creating the flexibility to enjoy your time off when it suits you

  • Certifications and training expensed

  • Life Assurance

  • Long Term Disability cover

  • Employee Assist Programme for employee advice and support (including legal and counselling helpline)

  • Health, Mental Health, Wellbeing, Financial and Legal support

  • 24/7 GP access

  • Pension auto-enrolment and contribution

  • Employee referral scheme

  • Client referral scheme

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Travel expenses policy

 

Interview Process

  1. Chat with Talent Team

  2. Remote interview with Hiring Manager

  3. Final in-person with Leadership Team

title: Head of Business Development, Investor Network
descriptionHtml:
We're hiring a business development leader to take over the team that builds and runs our investor network: six associates, one number, and a direct line to both co-founders.

Pairs is a vetted private capital network. We put breakout founders in front of the family offices, VCs and strategic investors who fit them, and those investors join our network as members. Founders pay for the access to those relationships and for the investor relations work our team does around every introduction, and that work is ultimately the product we sell.

The two co-founders have led this team themselves until now. It has grown to around six associates, which is past the point where two founders can coach it hands on while running the rest of the company, so we are hiring the person who takes it over.

The role
You lead the investor relations team and report to both co-founders. Each associate holds a book of investor members and runs several things at once, new investor relationships, the nurturing of existing ones, and the introductions we make for our clients, plus the follow-up work from there. Your job is to make that team excellent and keep it at full leverage, which means every associate knows what is expected, gets coached every week, can measure their own progress, and hears it the same day when something is off.

What you will do

  • Run the weekly rhythm, a pipeline and network review (CRM), a review of every win and loss, KPIs, and a one to one with every associate.

  • Coach every associate on their calls and their introductions.

  • Hire, onboard and, when needed, let people go, against a written bar for what good looks like.

  • Own the health of the entire Pairs network, more active members every month, and every member getting founders that fit at the pace they asked for.

  • Work with our client success team on each client's plan, so what your team works on matches what the client expects, and with our founder relations team, who build relationships with top founders long before they become clients.

  • Spot the constraint that holds the team back and fix it, with a process or together with our engineers, which takes someone who knows which problem is worth solving.

  • Bring the two co-founders the weekly numbers, investor calls, newly active members, introductions sent, founder calls and referrals, and what you are changing because of them.


What you bring

  • You have run a sales, business development or investment team of five or more for at least two years, the number you carried was the team's, and you can name what the team achieved under you and who you promoted.

  • People respected you and still wanted to work for you, without you needing to be liked. You give straight feedback and you hold the standard when it is uncomfortable.

  • Ego and politics are not part of how you work. You talk about the team's results before your own, and your last team would say the same about you.

  • Systems are how you think. You have built the CRM discipline, the reporting or the playbook that others then ran on, and you can find the one constraint in a team and remove it.

  • Incentives and retention make sense to you. You know what makes the right behavior pay and what makes a team stick together, and you have the retention to show for it.

  • You play the long game. You would not squeeze one month at the cost of the next three, and you go for quality over quantity with investors and founders alike.

  • The investor world is one you know well enough to coach. You have sold high ticket to senior buyers, raised capital, or built an investor or executive network yourself, and years in venture capital or at a fund are a plus on top of the team you led.


Backgrounds we expect to see are high ticket competitive sales, consulting, banking and investment teams. This is not the seat for a great dealmaker who has never led a team, our associate role is the right application for that, and investor relations at a listed company or LP reporting at a fund is a different job from this one.

What good looks like

  • By day 30 you have familiarized yourself closely with the associate work and what we expect from it.

  • Ninety days in, the weekly rhythm runs on your numbers and every associate has a written plan they measure themselves against.

  • Every month the network has more active members and every client's introductions went out on fit and on time.

  • Every quarter one constraint is gone from the team's way, through a process or through engineering.

  • After a year the associates have grown, and the relationships with investors and founders are stronger than they were, since everything here is built to compound over years.


Compensation and how we work
US$200K to US$300K+ total compensation, base plus a bonus on the team's results. Fully remote, your day overlaps with US Eastern time for a few hours. The best AI tooling is paid for, so the admin runs itself and your hours go to people. You work next to our client success lead, our founder relations team and our engineers, each of them running their own lane.

How to apply
Hit apply, which takes you to a short form with four questions. The two co-founders read every application. The process from there is a first call, final conversations with both co-founders, and three references.

No ego is the first rule here, the team's result comes before anyone's name, the co-founders included. And everything is built to compound, so every relationship and every number should be stronger next year than it is now.

title: Head of Corporate Communications (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
FASTR Energy gehört zu den führenden Energiedienstleistern und Stromversorgern in
Deutschland. Das Unternehmen wurde 1989 in Aachen gegründet und hat
heute seinen Hauptsitz in Düsseldorf sowie Niederlassungen in Berlin,
Hamburg, München und Leizpig. Aus einem ursprünglich familiengeführten
Unternehmen ist ein dynamischer Energiepartner geworden, der sich im Mai
2025 durch die Partnerschaft mit KKR auf einen klaren Wachstumskurs
begeben hat. In einer spannenden Transformationsphase gestalten wir
aktiv die Zukunft der Energieversorgung – mit einer klaren Vision: Als
Dekarbonisierungspartner der Immobilienwirtschaft leisten wir einen
entscheidenden Beitrag zur Energiewende in Deutschland.

Die Rolle

Als Head of Corporate Communications (mögliche Standorte Düsseldorf, Berlin, München oder Hamburg) verantwortest du die Kommunikation eines Unternehmens in einer prägenden Phase: FASTR ist als bundesweiter, integrierter Energiedienstleister für die Immobilienwirtschaft, Kommunen und Stadtwerke neu aufgestellt und wächst. Du baust die Kommunikationsfunktion strategisch auf und aus, gibst ihr Struktur und Handschrift und machst die Positionierung des Unternehmens nach innen und außen erlebbar.

Das ist ausdrücklich keine ausführende Kommunikationsrolle. Du gestaltest von Grund auf – mit direktem Zugang zur Geschäftsführung, unternehmensweiter Sichtbarkeit und dem Mandat, Themen zu setzen statt sie nur zu begleiten.

Deine Verantwortung

  • Du entwickelst die Kommunikationsstrategie des Unternehmens und führst interne wie externe Kommunikation zu einem konsistenten Auftritt zusammen.

  • Du verantwortest die Kommunikation gegenüber Kunden ebenso wie gegenüber Bewerbenden und Mitarbeitenden und sorgst dafür, dass alle Zielgruppen dieselbe Marke erleben.

  • Du berätst die Geschäftsführung als Sparringspartner in Kommunikationsfragen, übersetzt Strategie und Positionierung in klare Botschaften und bringst Themen aktiv ein.

  • Du machst technisch und regulatorisch geprägte Themen der Energie- und Immobilienwirtschaft für unterschiedliche Zielgruppen verständlich und positionierst das Unternehmen als verlässlichen Partner gegenüber Wohnungswirtschaft, Kommunen, Stadtwerken und institutionellen Investoren.

  • Du entwickelst in enger Abstimmung mit HR das Employer Branding von FASTR und machst uns als Arbeitgeber sichtbar – von den Karrierekanälen bis zur internen Kommunikation.

  • Du verantwortest die Presse- und Medienarbeit, baust Beziehungen zu relevanten Medien und Multiplikatoren auf und positionierst das Unternehmen zu den Themen der Energie- und Immobilienwirtschaft.

  • Du steuerst und erweiterst die Kommunikationskanäle – von LinkedIn bis zur Fachpresse – und entwickelst Formate, die zur Positionierung des Unternehmens passen.

  • Du steuerst die Zusammenarbeit von Corporate Communications und Sales Marketing und verantwortest die digitalen Marketingkampagnen – von Content über Social Media bis Performance Marketing – zur Unterstützung von Markenbekanntheit und Leadgenerierung.

  • Du schaffst die Grundlagen einer skalierbaren Kommunikationsfunktion: Prozesse, Guidelines, Standards und Strukturen, die mit dem Unternehmen mitwachsen.

  • Du führst ein kleines Team an der Schnittstelle von Kommunikation und Marketing, entwickelst es weiter und verzahnst beide Bereiche eng.

Das bringst du mit

Erforderlich

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Unternehmenskommunikation, davon nachweislich in einer gestaltenden oder aufbauenden Funktion.

  • Ausgeprägte Fähigkeit, komplexe, erklärungsbedürftige Sachverhalte klar, präzise und zielgruppengerecht zu vermitteln.

  • Erfahrung in der B2B- und Stakeholder-Kommunikation, idealerweise in einem technisch, industriell oder infrastrukturnah geprägten Umfeld.

  • Strategisches Denkvermögen kombiniert mit der Fähigkeit und Bereitschaft, Themen selbst operativ umzusetzen.

  • Sicheres, souveränes Auftreten gegenüber der Geschäftsführungsebene – du schaffst Klarheit und vertrittst deine fachliche Haltung überzeugend.

  • Fundierte Erfahrung in der Presse- und Medienarbeit.

  • Erfahrung in der Führung von Mitarbeitenden sowie die Bereitschaft, ein Team aufzubauen und weiterzuentwickeln.

Von Vorteil

  • Ein belastbares Netzwerk zu Medien und Fachöffentlichkeit.

  • Erfahrung in Marken- oder Integrationsphasen, etwa bei der Zusammenführung mehrerer Organisationen unter einer gemeinsamen Marke.

  • Erfahrung darin, eine neue oder sich entwickelnde Markenidentität kommunikativ zu tragen.

  • Nähe zu erklärungsbedürftigen Branchen wie Energie, Infrastruktur oder Immobilienwirtschaft.

  • Erfahrung im Employer Branding und Personalmarketing, idealerweise in enger Zusammenarbeit mit HR.

  • Erfahrung in der Steuerung digitaler Marketingkampagnen (z. B. Content-, Social-Media- und Performance-Marketing) sowie im Zusammenspiel mit Sales Marketing.

Was dich bei uns erwartet

  • Eine Aufbau- und Gestaltungsrolle mit echtem Mandat statt vorgegebener Routinen.

  • Direkter Draht zur Geschäftsführung und Einfluss auf die Außen- und Innenwahrnehmung des Unternehmens.

  • Ein Unternehmen in einer aktiven Wachstums- und Integrationsphase, in der Kommunikation strategisch gebraucht wird.

  • Die Möglichkeit, eine Kommunikationsfunktion nach eigenen Vorstellungen zu prägen und mit dem Unternehmen wachsen zu lassen.

  • Eine Aufgabe mit Sinn: Hinter deinen Botschaften stehen echte Anlagen, echte Kunden und ein Thema, das gesellschaftlich zählt.

  • Eine solide Basis: über 25 Jahre operative Erfahrung, rund 1.100 betriebene Heizzentralen und ein Investor im Rücken, der unser Wachstum trägt.

  • Ein Team im Zusammenwachsen: Aus drei Unternehmen wird eine Marke – und du prägst mit, wie sich das nach innen und außen anfühlt.

Warum diese Rolle?

Solche Ausgangslagen sind selten: eine etablierte operative Basis von über 25 Jahren, eine frisch geschärfte Marke und ein finanziell solide getragenes Wachstum. Wenn du Unternehmenskommunikation nicht verwalten, sondern gestalten und sichtbar Wirkung erzielen möchtest, findest du hier den Rahmen dafür – mit Verantwortung ab dem ersten Tag und dem Gestaltungsspielraum, eine Funktion von Grund auf zu prägen.
